title: Latency-aware staged deployments with tenant-priority preemption and localized shadowing
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Build a routing + fallback system for model variant rollouts that (1) gates by latency and quality signals in the canary, (2) applies per-tenant priority preemption when capacity tiers are constrained, and (3) supports localized shadowing in regions to validate compatibility without impacting production SLOs. This ticket covers design, implementation hooks in the runtime, and an operator-facing rollout policy UI integration.
acceptance_criteria: Canary traffic can be configured with latency and quality gates: p50/p95 token latency thresholds, error-rate, and eval-set quality score delta.

When Dedicated capacity tier saturates, the router can preempt lower-priority tenant traffic in favor of higher-priority tenants according to tenant priority labels stored in the customer config service.

Regional shadowing mode can mirror N% of production requests to a variant within the same region with safe KV-cache isolation and no downstream side-effects (requests must be idempotent or marked as dry-run).
Automatic rollback triggers: canary failure on any gate or sustained regression for 3m with autoretry/backoff. Rollback recorded to audit log and fires alert to oncall.

E2E test harness demonstrates staged rollout across two regions with simulated capacity loss in primary region and successful failover to secondary with no SLA violations for high-priority tenants in the simulation.
Console UI shows tenant-priority distribution, current preemption events, and per-region compatibility verdicts for each variant rollout.

comments: 2025-02-11 Maya Patel: Initial spec drafted. Key trade-off: whether preemption should be enforced by router (fast, coarse) or by per-worker admission (fine-grained, more complexity). Recommended approach: router-level preemption with a fallback per-worker token bucket for safety.

2025-02-12 Owen Ramirez: Reviewed design; noted risk that tenant-priority labels must be immutable for the duration of a rollout to avoid oscillation. Suggest adding a TTL lock on priority changes during active rollouts.

2025-02-14 Lina (Design): Console mockups added to Confluence; emphasized the need for clear UX to show 'preempted tenants' vs 'failed canary' states so operators do not confuse capacity preemption for model regressions.

2025-02-15 Kendra: Began runtime preemption hook. Ran local perf bench; initial implementation adds ~0.3% CPU overhead but warms the routing cache. Filing small follow-up for kernel-level optimization.

2025-02-17 Sam: Simulation harness ready; initial run shows canary gate catches p95 latency regressions for long-context prompts. Simulated Dedicated pool saturation correctly preempted lowest-priority tenants in 90% of trials; investigating outliers.

2025-02-18 Security: Quick review flagged that shadowing must not send PII to downstream logging endpoints. Added requirement: shadowed requests are tagged and scrubbed before any external side effects (billing hooks, third-party logs).

2025-02-19 Owen Ramirez: PR opened for routing changes: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/942-fallback-preemption. Added integration tests for regional shadowing. Requesting review from Kendra + Infra.
2025-02-20 PM (Eleanor): Decomposed rollout plan in Cycle 2025-W07: canary window 90m, automatic rollback + alerting threshold set, identify top-20 high-priority tenants to monitor during rollout.

2025-02-20 Maya Patel: Noted blocker: two Dedicated customers require contractual guarantees; we need a migration plan if preemption would violate committed SLAs. Added dependency on legal/enterprise-ops.
2025-02-20 Owen Ramirez: Added temporary mitigation: honor 'sla-exempt' flag to never preempt tenants with dedicated SLA contracts; will add audit to ensure correctness.
2025-02-20 QA: Planning synthetic experiments to validate that shadowing does not change production caches; using isolated KV prefixes per shadow run.
notes: Falls under broader Model Lifecycle initiative. Keep TTL lock for tenant-priority changes during active rollout. Consider follow-up to support gradual degradation ladder instead of binary preemption.
audit_trail: 2025-02-19 PR opened by Owen: runtime change + integration tests
